handbook.birdwatch.little_egret.name: Little Egret
handbook.birdwatch.little_egret.habitat: Habits: Forages slowly along shallow shorelines and mudflats, elegant yet alert; active by day, roosts in trees or reeds at dusk, flies off when startled.
handbook.birdwatch.little_egret.tip: Tip: Ambush riverside shallows while sneaking; alarm distance is about 8 blocks. Use a 200mm+ tele lens from 20m away; focus on the eye and keep shutter at 1/500s or faster to freeze the wingbeat.
handbook.birdwatch.sparrow.name: Tree Sparrow
handbook.birdwatch.sparrow.habitat: Habits: The most common bird in villages and farmlands; gathers in flocks, hops and pecks on the ground, not very shy of people. Active by day, roosts under eaves or in bushes at night.
handbook.birdwatch.sparrow.tip: Tip: Sparrows have a very short alarm distance - a 50mm lens works. Catch them pecking on the ground at 1/250s or faster; sit still by the village entrance and let them come to you.
handbook.birdwatch.tit.name: Great Tit
handbook.birdwatch.tit.habitat: Habits: A lively little bird of forests and woodland edges; hops among canopy branches foraging, sometimes drops to the ground. Active by day with a crisp call.
handbook.birdwatch.tit.tip: Tip: Great Tits never stop hopping in the canopy - use a 200mm+ lens, lock focus and track. Shutter at 1/500s or faster; they are most active at dawn.

bestiary.birdwatch.cow.desc: Docile livestock that graze the plains in herds. A good shot captures pastoral life.
bestiary.birdwatch.sheep.desc: Woolly grazers whose fleece can be sheared. They wander the hills and meadows.
bestiary.birdwatch.pig.desc: Pink livestock that root through the dirt. Pigs napping in the sun are photogenic.
bestiary.birdwatch.chicken.desc: Common poultry that peck around villages and farms. Hens lay eggs, roosters crow.
bestiary.birdwatch.horse.desc: Tall riding animals with many coat variants. Their gallop is graceful.
bestiary.birdwatch.donkey.desc: Stubborn pack animals, shorter than horses, often carrying chests.
bestiary.birdwatch.rabbit.desc: Nimble grazers that bound across plains and taigas. Extremely wary up close.
bestiary.birdwatch.cat.desc: Common mousers in villages with varied coats. Strays are most active at night.
bestiary.birdwatch.wolf.desc: Pack hunters of forests and taigas. Wild wolves are cautious and dangerous.
bestiary.birdwatch.fox.desc: Red-coated nocturnal hunters of forests and taigas. Best seen at dusk and dawn.
bestiary.birdwatch.goat.desc: Mountain climbers that leap across cliffs. They like to headbutt passersby.
bestiary.birdwatch.bat.desc: Nocturnal fliers of caves, using echolocation. They roost upside down by day.
bestiary.birdwatch.parrot.desc: Vivid tropical birds that mimic player speech. They dwell in jungle canopies.
bestiary.birdwatch.axolotl.desc: Smiling water spirits of lush caves. Found in pink, blue, yellow and more.
bestiary.birdwatch.frog.desc: Leaping hunters of wetlands that eat small insects. Temperate, cold and tropical variants.
bestiary.birdwatch.turtle.desc: Slow, leisurely elders of the beach. Hatchlings crawl toward the sea.
bestiary.birdwatch.squid.desc: Soft-bodied sea creatures with ten arms. They ink the dark waters at night.
bestiary.birdwatch.cod.desc: Common cold-water fish that swim in schools. Reliable food for sea travelers.
bestiary.birdwatch.salmon.desc: Anadromous fish that leap waterfalls upstream. They run in rivers during spawning.
bestiary.birdwatch.tropical_fish.desc: Vivid little fish in countless shapes and colors. Coral reefs are their home.
bestiary.birdwatch.zombie.desc: Undead wanderers of the night that fear sunlight. They burn at dawn.
bestiary.birdwatch.skeleton.desc: Precise archers of the night and caves. Bones are their armor.
bestiary.birdwatch.spider.desc: Eight-legged night hunters that scale walls. Watch for their eyes in the dark.
bestiary.birdwatch.creeper.desc: A green creature that creeps close, then explodes. Keep your distance!
screen.birdwatch.bestiary.no_desc: A recorded creature. Habitat notes coming soon.
